headline: 2026 Uncertainty-Aware ML study: Logistic Regression Brier 0.199 (BELOW our 0.20 target), XGBoost 0.202 — both better than fleet best 0.22062

sources.title: Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning for NBA Forecasting in Digital Betting Markets

key_results.best_model: LSTM + Monte Carlo dropout at inference

sources.title: Machine Learning for Basketball Game Outcomes: NBA and WNBA Leagues
Comparing Machine Learning Methods for NBA Game Outcome Prediction

key_insight: Logistic Regression with proper feature selection achieves Brier 0.199 in 2026 SOTA — beating our target of 0.20 AND beating XGBoost (0.202). This directly validates P7 (our logistic_regression political island, most stable) and argues for adding a logistic_regression NBA island.

relevance_to_fleet.S17_xgboost: XGBoost achieves 0.202 in SOTA (vs our S17 best 0.22249). Gap = 0.020. Indicates our XGBoost features/tuning has room. Feature engineering quality is the bottleneck, not model choice.
relevance_to_fleet.S13_S15_extra_trees: Extra Trees not benchmarked in 2026 study. CNN achieves 0.221 (comparable to our 0.22062 fleet best). Suggests extra_trees may be near its ceiling.
relevance_to_fleet.P7_logistic: Political P7 uses logistic_regression, is the most STABLE island (686 gens/h, no OOM crashes). 2026 study confirms LR is competitive. P7's 0.25412 brier gap from 0.199 is ENTIRELY feature engineering.
relevance_to_fleet.new_island_proposal: Add logistic_regression NBA island. Would use same feature engine, different model. Historical evidence: LR = most stable + calibrated. Zero extra memory vs XGBoost.

actionable_techniques.name: Monte Carlo Dropout Calibration Head
actionable_techniques.description: Wrap tree ensemble predictions with MC dropout during inference to generate uncertainty estimates. On CPU: run predict_proba() N=30 times with bootstrap resampling to simulate MC dropout.
actionable_techniques.cpu_adaptation: Bootstrap predict_proba() over 30 random feature subsets (already done by RandomForest, but explicit uncertainty = std across trees). ExtraTrees: use estimators list, take std as uncertainty.
actionable_techniques.implementation_loc: features/engine.py evaluate_individual() — wrap y_pred with calibration step

actionable_techniques.name: Isotonic Calibration Post-Processing
actionable_techniques.description: sklearn.calibration.CalibratedClassifierCV(method='isotonic', cv=3) wrapper on ExtraTrees/XGBoost. Already proposed in sota-2026-04-27-16h.json. Re-confirming: this is the highest-ROI technique.

actionable_techniques.name: Add Logistic Regression NBA Island
actionable_techniques.description: Replace the paused S18 (TESTforge42/nba-evo-s18, stale 9 days) with a logistic_regression variant. 2026 SOTA achieves 0.199 with LR. Zero OOM risk, stable, fast.
actionable_techniques.rationale: S18 already stale 9 days. If checkpoint is broken, restart from scratch with LR. LR trains 10x faster than ExtraTrees per generation — more gens/h.

actionable_techniques.name: Rolling Feature Importance Pruning
actionable_techniques.description: Every 100 gens, recompute feature importance and drop bottom 20%. Prevents feature bloat as GA adds features. Matches paper's emphasis on feature selection quality over model complexity.
actionable_techniques.implementation_loc: GA mutate() / crossover() in HF space app.py

fleet_context.gap_interpretation: Our gap to 2026 SOTA is entirely attributable to: (1) CPU-only constraint (no LSTM/deep learning), (2) feature engineering quality, (3) lack of calibration post-processing. Calibration alone (isotonic) should close ~0.005 gap.
